text:
Incident-Bot: paging @Sam (oncall) — elevated 5xx + timeouts for /v1/streaming across eu-west-1 and us-west-2. Alert ALERT-2026-304.

Sam: on it. hitting dashboards now. are these from synthetic checks or customer traffic?

Incident-Bot: mixed. synthetic probes and increased 5xx fronting real customer sessions. sample customer: acme-inc (session trace id: s-trace-7f9c).

Sam: copying gateway logs snapshot:
```
2026-03-15T02:10:41Z ERROR ingress: upstream 502 incomplete chunk read while proxying /v1/streaming client_id=acme-inc session=s-trace-7f9c
2026-03-15T02:10:42Z WARN  ingress: client cancel detected: ECONNRESET from 10.4.2.19
2026-03-15T02:10:43Z ERROR router: gateway timeout to runtime pool: deadline exceeded to 10.5.8.22
2026-03-15T02:10:44Z ERROR runtime: worker OOM while serving stream chunk write
```

Sam: hypothesis: runtime under backpressure causing partial chunk streams + gateway's chunked proxy doesn't gracefully handle mid-stream EOS. Also seeing sudden spike in client disconnects.

Anjali: CS reports multiple customers seeing truncated streams and no reconnect. impact severity?

CS-Bot: Acme ticket #5912: "stream stops ~10s in with 502, no reconnect or error body". Severity: P2 for now, increasing if more customers.

Ravi: I'll take over oncall in ~8m. grabbing kube access and tracing.

Sam: immediate mitigations I want to try (low-risk first):
- flip ingress route to buffered streaming (disable chunked proxy) for /v1/streaming
- bump gateway proxy read timeout to 45s (was 15s)
- scale runtime-pool-1 by +30%
- collect runtime heap/proc stats and pstack of workers

Infra-Bot: autoscaler already added +3 nodes to runtime-pool-1 at 02:12:07Z (policy: spike-protect).

Sam: applying route flag now. command:
```bash
kubectl -n infra patch configmap routing-policies --type=json -p '[{"op":"add","path":"/data/streaming-buffered-fallback","value":"true"}]'
kubectl rollout restart deployment/ingress-gateway -n infra
```

Deploy-Bot: rollout started for ingress-gateway at 02:12:35Z (rev v2026.03.15-219).

Liz: FYI toggling to buffered will increase latency and memory per connection — might raise costs but should reduce mid-stream truncation.

Sam: increasing gateway timeouts now (live patch):
```bash
kubectl -n infra patch configmap ingress-proxy --type=json -p '[{"op":"replace","path":"/data/proxy_read_timeout","value":"45s"}]'
```

Sam: live patch applied. monitoring logs.

Ryan: started collecting runtime logs + pprof for the affected pool. attaching debug snapshot to thread. found a pattern: many workers stuck in syscall write() awaiting socket drain, kernel buffers full.

Sam: that maps to backpressure. can we temporarily enable accept-throttling on gateway so it sheds new streaming connections?

Ravi: implementing a soft reject (429) for new streams on ingress in eu-west-1 to reduce backlog. command:
```bash
kubectl -n infra exec deploy/ingress-rate-limiter -- curl -s -XPOST http://localhost/config -d '{"stream_limit": 1200}'
```

Anjali: CS — please inform affected customers of mitigation steps and ask them to retry. Any broad customer-facing incidents will need a status page update.

CS-Bot: Notifying Acme with temp mitigation (buffered streaming + retries). Ticket updated 02:14:10Z.

Sam: still seeing occasional 502s but rate is dropping. extracting a failing trace: s-trace-7f9c shows chunked frames stop after 9.8s with no final chunk and gateway logs show upstream reset. grabbing tcpdump from runtime host 10.5.8.22.

Ryan: tcpdump shows FIN from runtime process immediately after a large write attempt. size of last chunk ~128KB. looks like runtime crashed OOM on large buffer flush.

Sam: that explains partial frames. any recent deploys to runtime?

Deploy-Bot: runtime pool rollout v2026.03.15-214 completed 01:58Z (no failures reported).

Sam: suspicious timing. check runtime memory flags and quantization config.

Ravi: found worker logs showing frequent GC spikes and bursts of memory > container limit before OOM kill. suspect a change in batching leading to larger KV cache growth.

Anjali: can we roll runtime back to previous revision while we investigate memory growth?

Sam: yes — low-risk rollback to v2026.03.14-198.

Deploy-Bot: initiating rollback for runtime-pool-1 at 02:18:12Z.

Infra-Bot: rollback succeeded, new nodes draining old pods, traffic shifting.

Sam: after rollback, 5xx rate dropped to baseline in us-west-2 and eu-west-1. buffered fallback still enabled for safety for 30m.

Ryan: confirm: packet traces show no more abrupt FINs from runtime. memory profiles look stable now.

Anjali: customer impact summary for postmortem: Acme and 2 other customers experienced truncated streams (502/TIMEOUT) for ~20m window starting 02:10Z. Root cause: memory growth in runtime worker after recent runtime rollout causing OOMs and partial writes; gateway's chunked proxy amplified symptom by passing incomplete frames instead of failing fast.

Sam: next steps (action items):
- infra: add graceful chunk validation in gateway to fail fast on incomplete frames (owner: Sam)
- runtime: add memory regression test for batching + KV cache growth (owner: Ryan)
- deploy: add canary latency/memory monitors before full rollout (owner: Deploy team)
- cs: follow up with impacted customers and offer a post-incident RCA (owner: Anjali)

Ravi: oncall handoff complete. leaving monitoring + pager for next rotation.

Sam: closing live mitigation window. keeping buffered fallback for 30m then revert if stable. will file incident and postmortem. :white_check_mark:
